where: Section 1, sentence 'The outputs are the fuel metering valve, variable stator vanes, bleed valves, ignition and the thrust reverser'
problem: A hydro-mechanical fuel control unit (FCU) is a fuel-metering device. It does not switch the ignition system and does not command the thrust reverser; on these engines ignition and reversal are separate systems. Students will wrongly learn that the FCU drives ignition and the reverser.
fix: List only the fuel metering valve, variable stator vanes and bleed valves as FCU outputs. Add: ignition and the thrust reverser are separate systems on a hydro-mechanical engine; on a FADEC engine the ignition is driven by the FADEC.

where: Section 1, sentence on EGT and TGT
problem: EGT and TGT are not 'the same limit'. They are the same kind of temperature measured at different stations involving the turbine, so the two limits have different numerical values and are not interchangeable.
fix: Say: EGT is the exhaust gas temperature; TGT (turbine gas temperature) is the same kind of measurement taken closer to the turbine, so its limiting value differs from the EGT limit.

problem: Stating flatly that the thrust parameter is N1 is only true for most turbofans. Other engines use N2 or engine pressure ratio (EPR) as the thrust-setting parameter, and a student may think N1 is universal.
fix: Add: most turbofans use N1, some engines use N2 or the engine pressure ratio (EPR) as the thrust-setting parameter; the rest of the loop is the same.

problem: The sensors node note reads 'P1, T1, N2, EGT' and leaves out N1, but the caption and the aria text say the sensors return N1, N2 and EGT. The feedback path therefore contradicts the figure's own description.
fix: Change the note to 'P1, T1, N1, N2, EGT'.
